sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: UPPER FLOW ACROSS NORTH AMERICA WILL REMAIN AMPLIFIED TODAY. A SUBTROPICAL HIGH IS EXPECTED TO REMAIN PROMINENT OVER THE GREAT BASIN...WITH A RIDGE EXTENDING NORTHWARD ALONG AN AXIS INTO THE LEE OF THE CANADIAN ROCKIES. ON THE WESTERN PERIPHERY OF THIS FEATURE...WEAK UPPER TROUGHING EMERGING FROM THE SUBTROPICAL EASTERN PACIFIC IS FORECAST TO CONTINUE DEVELOPING NORTHWARD NEAR THE CALIFORNIA COAST. AT THE SAME TIME...A SIGNIFICANT IMPULSE WITHIN THE MID-LATITUDE WESTERLIES APPEARS LIKELY TO DIG AROUND ITS NORTHEASTERN PERIPHERY...ACROSS THE CENTRAL CANADIAN/U.S. BORDER AREA...INTO LARGE-SCALE UPPER TROUGHING CURVING ACROSS THE MISSISSIPPI VALLEY INTO THE ATLANTIC SEABOARD. A MUCH STRONGER DOWNSTREAM IMPULSE IS FORECAST TO GRADUALLY PIVOT THROUGH THE OHIO VALLEY...AND ADJACENT PORTIONS OF THE LOWER GREAT LAKES REGION AND CENTRAL APPALACHIANS. MODELS CONTINUE TO INDICATE THAT THIS WILL BE ACCOMPANIED BY SIGNIFICANT LOW/MID-LEVEL CYCLOGENESIS ACROSS THE UPPER OHIO VALLEY AND LOWER GREAT LAKES REGION DURING THE DAY TODAY. SECONDARY SURFACE LOW DEVELOPMENT IS PROBABLE TO THE LEE OF THE NORTH CENTRAL APPALACHIANS TONIGHT...AS THE UPPER IMPULSE TAKES ON MORE OF A NEUTRAL TO NEGATIVE TILT.

sections.title: MID ATLANTIC COAST/UPPER OHIO VALLEY/CENTRAL APPALACHIANS
sections.text: THE EVOLVING LARGE-SCALE PATTERN DOES APPEAR AT LEAST SOMEWHAT CONDUCIVE TO CONSIDERABLE CONVECTIVE POTENTIAL FOR TODAY...PARTICULARLY IN TERMS OF FORCING FOR LARGE-SCALE ASCENT AND SUFFICIENT VERTICAL SHEAR IN THE WARM SECTOR OF THE DEVELOPING CYCLONE. THE WARM SECTOR...PARTICULARLY EAST OF THE CENTRAL APPALACHIANS...LIKELY WILL BECOME CHARACTERIZED BY SEASONABLY HIGH MOISTURE CONTENT. HOWEVER...MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES ARE NOT EXPECTED TO BE PARTICULARLY STEEP...RESULTING IN RATHER MODEST CAPE...AND MODELS SUGGEST THAT STRONGEST 850 MB WIND FIELDS MAY BE CONFINED TO THE COOL SIDE OF THE WARM FRONTAL ZONE. THE FRONT INITIALLY WILL EXTEND ACROSS THE UPPER OHIO VALLEY INTO NORTHERN MID ATLANTIC COAST...AND APPEARS LIKELY TO BE REINFORCED BY WIDESPREAD PRECIPITATION DURING THE DAY TODAY. LOW-LEVEL HODOGRAPHS THROUGH MUCH OF THE WARM SECTOR MAY REMAIN WEAK TO MODEST IN STRENGTH...PERHAPS LARGEST NEAR A LINGERING SURFACE BOUNDARY ACROSS NORTHERN VIRGINIA INTO THE DELMARVA PENINSULA...AND NEAR THE SURFACE CYCLONE OVER EASTERN OHIO/WESTERN PENNSYLVANIA...BEFORE IT OCCLUDES. THE HIGHER BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE CONTENT EXPECTED EAST OF THE LEE SURFACE TROUGH...ACROSS NORTHERN/EASTERN VIRGINIA

sections.title: NORTHERN PLAINS RED RIVER VALLEY
sections.text: MODEST BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTENING...COUPLED WITH STEEPENING OF MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES ASSOCIATED WITH THE APPROACHING DIGGING SHORT WAVE IMPULSE...PROBABLY WILL CONTRIBUTE TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF VIGOROUS THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT BY LATE AFTERNOON. STRENGTHENING OF NORTH NORTHWESTERLY 500 MB FLOW TO 40+ KT WILL ENHANCE THE SEVERE WEATHER POTENTIAL...WITH A COUPLE OF SUPERCELLS POSSIBLE...CAPABLE OF PRODUCING LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING SURFACE GUSTS. IT IS POSSIBLE THAT FORCING FOR UPWARD VERTICAL MOTION MAY BE SUFFICIENT TO SUPPORT CONSOLIDATION AND UPSCALE GROWTH OF CONVECTION INTO A SOUTHWARD ADVANCING ORGANIZED CLUSTER OF STORMS...BEFORE ACTIVITY WEAKENS THIS EVENING.

sections.title: INTERMOUNTAIN WEST/ROCKIES
sections.text: STEEP LOWER/MID TROPOSPHERIC LAPSE RATES...SUFFICIENT MOISTURE... AND LARGE-SCALE FORCING FOR ASCENT ASSOCIATED WITH IMPULSES MIGRATING AROUND THE PERIPHERY OF THE SUBTROPICAL RIDGE ARE EXPECTED TO CONTRIBUTE TO THUNDERSTORM ACTIVITY TODAY. THIS APPEARS MOST LIKELY ON THE SOUTHERN PERIPHERY OF THE RIDGE...ACROSS THE NORTHERN ROCKIES INTO THE LOWER DESERTS OF ARIZONA...AND ACROSS THE NORTHWESTERN PERIPHERY...TO THE EAST OF THE SOUTHERN CASCADES...WHERE STRONGEST STORMS MAY BE ACCOMPANIED BY STRONG WIND GUSTS AND SOME HAIL. ..KERR/LEITMAN.. 06/27/2015

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: PNA PATTERN ALOFT IS WELL-ESTABLISHED NOW AND SHOULD PERSIST THROUGH PERIOD...WITH HIGH-AMPLITUDE RIDGING OVER WRN NORTH AMERICA AND CYCLONIC FLOW OVER MOST OF ERN CONUS. STG MID/UPPER-LEVEL ANTICYCLONE CENTERED OVER GREAT BASIN REGION AND BROAD CYCLONE WELL OFFSHORE CA WILL DOMINATE FLOW FROM ROCKIES WWD. MEANWHILE...COMPACT 500-MB CYCLONE IS APPARENT OVER NRN INDIANA/SRN LOWER MI...WITH TROUGHING SWWD ACROSS E TX. THIS CYCLONE SHOULD PIVOT SLOWLY ACROSS LAKE ERIE REGION THROUGH PERIOD. ASSOCIATED SFC LOW SHOULD DEEPEN AND MOVE SLOWLY NEWD OVER OH WHILE OCCLUDING...EVENTUALLY BECOMING STACKED WITH MID/UPPER CYCLONE. WARM FRONT...WHICH HAS BEEN OBSCURED OVERNIGHT BY SEVERAL OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES AND PRECIP AREAS...IS EVIDENT FROM LOW SEWD ACROSS SRN WV THEN EWD ROUGHLY OVER VA/NC BORDER REGION. THIS FRONT WILL MOVE NEWD ACROSS VA TODAY INTO AT LEAST POTOMAC RIVER REGION AND ADJOINING PORTIONS OF MD...AND PERHAPS AS FAR N AS SRN PA. WEAK/SECONDARY LOW DEVELOPMENT IS POSSIBLE ALONG WARM FRONT OVER NRN VA/NWRN MD VICINITY STARTING AROUND 00Z. MEANWHILE...NRN-STREAM SHORTWAVE TROUGH IS EVIDENT IN MOISTURE-CHANNEL IMAGERY OVER SK/MB BORDER...AND IS FCST TO AMPLIFY AS IT MOVES SEWD ACROSS S

sections.title: CENTRAL APPALACHIANS/MID ATLANTIC/UPPER OH VALLEY
sections.text: SVR POTENTIAL OVER THIS REGION WILL EVENTUALLY OVERLAP SOMEWHAT BUT LARGELY WILL DEPEND ON TWO CORRIDORS OF PROBABLE DIURNAL DESTABILIZATION -- 1. BETWEEN ONGOING CONVECTIVE/PRECIP PLUMES OVER NRN VA/MD/DELMARVA AND OVER OH/WV. LOW-LEVEL WARM ADVECTION AND MOISTURE TRANSPORT WILL OCCUR IN CONCERT WITH NWD SHIFT OF WARM FRONTAL ZONE ACROSS THIS REGION...CONTRIBUTING ENOUGH THETAE TO YIELD PATCHES OF 1500-2000 J/KG MLCAPE. RICH LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE ALSO SHOULD KEEP LCL RELATIVELY LOW...IN REGION OF BACKED SFC WINDS AND RELATIVELY MAXIMIZED STORM-RELATIVE BOUNDARY-LAYER FLOW NEAR WARM FRONT. GIVEN FAVORABLE AMBIENT DEEP SHEAR FOR SUPERCELLS AND RATHER LARGE LOW-LEVEL HODOGRAPHS -- FEATURING 0-1-KM SRN 200-400 J/KG COLLOCATED WITH SFC-BASED EFFECTIVE-INFLOW PARCELS -- SOME OF THOSE SUPERCELLS SHOULD PRODUCE TORNADOES...ESPECIALLY NEAR WARM FRONT THIS AFTN INTO EARLY EVENING. TORNADO PROBABILITIES ACCORDINGLY HAVE BEEN RAISED A NOTCH AND CONCENTRATED WITHIN THAT REGIME...WHICH DOES INCLUDE I-95 CORRIDOR IN NRN VA/DC/MD. DAMAGING GUSTS ALSO ARE LIKELY...MOST DENSE POTENTIAL BEING OVER 30% WIND AREA WHERE BOWING LINES...SUPERCELLS AND MULTICELLULAR CLUSTERS EACH WILL OFFER THAT THREAT. ISOL

sections.title: UPPER MIDWEST/NRN PLAINS
sections.text: TSTMS MAY DEVELOP AS EARLY AS MIDDAY ALONG/AHEAD OF SFC COLD FRONT AND BECOME WIDELY SCATTERED TO SCATTERED THROUGH LATE AFTN...WHILE SPREADING SSEWD. LARGE HAIL AND SPORADIC DAMAGING GUSTS ARE POSSIBLE...WITH SFC HEATING AND DEW POINTS MID 50S TO NEAR 60 F CONTRIBUTING TO WELL-MIXED SUBCLOUD LAYERS...WEAK CINH AND 1000-2000 J/KG MLCAPE. NEAR-SFC WINDS MOSTLY WILL BE AOB 10 KT AND HAVE DOMINANT WLY COMPONENT...BUT WITH SUBSTANTIAL DIRECTIONAL SHEAR UNDER STG MID-UPPER NWLYS. THIS WILL CONTRIBUTE TO LONG HODOGRAPHS AND EFFECTIVE-SHEAR MAGNITUDES 30-40 KT. ISOLATED 2-INCH HAIL CANNOT BE RULED OUT...GIVEN STEEPNESS OF LAPSE RATES ALOFT AND POTENTIAL EVAPOTRANSPIRATIVE BOOST TO IMPLIED CLOUD-WATER CONTENT IN ENVIRONMENT FAVORING AT LEAST A FEW SUPERCELLS. ANALOG DATA AND FCST SOUNDINGS WITH 2-D HAIL MODEL APPLIED EACH SUGGEST DOMINANCE OF EVENTS MEASURING IN 1-1.75 INCH RANGE BUT WITH LARGER HAIL POSSIBLE UNDER ONLY SLGT MODIFICATION. NAM APPEARS TO REPRESENT UPPER END OF FAVORABLE INFLOW-LAYER MOISTENING ACROSS THIS AREA...A COMMON BIAS IN THAT MODEL. FOR NOW POTENTIAL APPEARS TOO CONDITIONAL FOR AOA-15%/SIG AREA.

sections.title: SWRN CONUS
sections.text: WIDELY SCATTERED TSTMS SHOULD FORM TODAY OVER HIGHER TERRAIN AND MOVE GENERALLY IN ALIGNMENT WITH FLOW ENCIRCLING MID/UPPER-LEVEL ANTICYCLONE -- I.E. TOWARD S OVER NRN NM AND WWD OVER SRN AZ. MOST INTENSE CELLS OVER NM MRGL AREA MAY PRODUCE STG TO SVR GUSTS...AND ISOLATED HAIL NEAR SVR LIMITS IS POSSIBLE MOSTLY IN NM PORTION WHERE CONVECTION MAY REMAIN MORE DISCRETE OVER HIGHER ELEVATIONS. CLOUD COVER FROM EARLIER CONVECTION MAY PERSIST OVER PARTS OF SRN NM AND SERN/EXTREME S-CENTRAL AZ NEAR NM BORDER...DELAYING/REDUCING HEATING RELATIVE TO AREAS FARTHER W AND NW. OBSERVED TUS RAOB CONTAINED ROUGHLY 95TH PERCENTILE OF PW VERSUS CLIMATOLOGY...AND POCKETS OF STG DIABATIC HEATING ARE EXPECTED AROUND HIGH-CLOUD FRAGMENTS THIS AFTN. FCST SOUNDINGS SUGGEST DEPTH OF ELY FLOW ALONG AND NE OF MOGOLLON RIM...WHILE NOT OPTIMAL...IS SUFFICIENT TO ENCOURAGE STORM MOTION OFF RIM AND INTO DESERTS. THERE...MUCH DEEPER TROPOSPHERIC ELYS -- POTENTIALLY OCCUPYING MOST OF 300-850-MB LAYER -- WILL AID WWD MOTION AND POTENTIAL FOR FORWARD-PROPAGATING CLUSTERS. TSTMS MAY PRODUCE LARGE OUTFLOW/HABOOB ARCS WITH EMBEDDED/LOCALLY DAMAGING GUSTS.

sections.title: GA TO GULF COAST STATES
sections.text: SCATTERED TSTMS WILL FORM THIS AFTN AND INTO EVENING AMIDST RICH LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE AND LIFT -- MOSTLY ALONG PREFRONTAL BOUNDARIES SUCH AS TROUGHS...OUTFLOWS...DIFFERENTIAL-HEATING ZONES...CONFLUENCE LINES...AND SEA BREEZES. STG HEATING AND SFC DEW POINTS 70S F WILL OFFSET MODEST LAPSE RATES ALOFT TO YIELD 2000-3000 J/KG MLCAPE. BEING OFF SRN RIM OF STRONGEST FLOW ALOFT...DEEP SHEAR WILL BE WEAK...AND VEERED NEAR-SFC WNDS WILL LIMIT LOW-LEVEL SHEAR AS WELL. AS SUCH...MOSTLY MULTICELL/PULSE MODES ARE EXPECTED...WITH SPORADIC WET DOWNBURSTS AND MRGL HAIL POSSIBLE.

sections.title: ORE...FAR NRN CA
sections.text: SCATTERED TSTMS SHOULD FORM THIS AFTN AMIDST STG HEATING OF HIGHER TERRAIN AND FAVORABLE LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE. VERY DEEP/WELL-MIXED BOUNDARY LAYERS ARE EVIDENT IN FCST SOUNDINGS OVER RELATIVELY LOW ELEVATIONS...BENEATH HIGHLY VARIABLE MLCAPES MAXING OUT AROUND 1000 J/KG. DAMAGING GUSTS ARE POSSIBLE FROM A FEW MORE INTENSE CELLS. WHATEVER HAIL REACHES SFC SHOULD BE MOSTLY SUB-SVR BUT AN ISOLATED EVENT AROUND AN INCH MAY OCCUR. REF SPC FIRE-WEATHER OUTLOOK FOR RELATED DRY-TSTM CONCERNS AND ADDITIONAL CONVECTIVE DISCUSSION FOR THIS REGION. ..EDWARDS/ROGERS.. 06/27/2015

sections.text: NO PARTICULARLY SUBSTANTIAL CHANGES HAVE BEEN MADE TO THE ONGOING FORECAST. mesoscale_discussions.discussion: VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY SHOWS CLEARING OVER PARTS OF ERN VA AND ESPECIALLY NC WITH A VERY WARM AND MOIST AIR MASS IN PLACE. SELY LOW-LEVEL FLOW WILL ADD TO THE DESTABILIZATION VIA THETA-E ADVECTION ACROSS THE REGION AND FARTHER N INTO MD LATE THIS AFTERNOON. AS THE SURFACE LOW DEEPENS TO THE W...LOW-LEVEL FLOW IS EXPECTED TO BACK AND STRENGTHEN FURTHER...WHICH WILL MAINTAIN FAVORABLE LOW-LEVEL SRH ALONG THE DIFFUSE WARM FRONT FOR SUPERCELLS AND TORNADOES GIVEN AMPLE MOISTURE AND INSTABILITY IN PLACE. IT IS POSSIBLE THAT SEVERE STORM COVERAGE ALONG THE WARM FRONT WILL BE ISOLATED. HOWEVER...STORMS THAT DO FULLY TAKE ADVANTAGE OF THE EXISTING LOW-LEVEL SHEAR WHILST HAVING INFLOW ROOTED IN THE HIGHER-CAPE AIR MASS WILL HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO PRODUCE TORNADOES.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SEVERE HAIL IS EXPECTED FROM SWRN VA ACROSS NC AND INTO NRN SC THIS AFTERNOON. LOCALIZED WIND DAMAGE MAY ALSO OCCUR.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: RADAR AND SATELLITE SHOW STORMS GRADUALLY INCREASING ACROSS THE WRN CAROLINAS AHEAD OF THE COLD FRONT AND BENEATH MODERATELY STRONG MID TO HIGH LEVEL WINDS. MODERATE INSTABILITY HAS DEVELOPED DUE TO HEATING ACROSS THE REGION...ESPECIALLY ACROSS SC AND WRN NC WHERE TEMPERATURES ARE WARMEST. AS THE INFLUENCE OF THE UPPER TROUGH INCREASES THIS AFTERNOON...STORMS SHOULD BECOME MORE INTENSE AND ORGANIZED. THE MOST FAVORABLE AREA FOR SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF LARGE HAIL AND WIND WILL BE BENEATH THE STRONGER MIDLEVEL FLOW FROM VA INTO NC. OTHER MORE ISOLATED SEVERE ACTIVITY IS EXPECTED POINTS S.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SEVERE THREAT IS INCREASING OVER EASTERN ND AND NORTHWEST MN. SUPERCELL THUNDERSTORMS...ACCOMPANIED BY LARGE HAIL...DAMAGING WINDS...AND PERHAPS A BRIEF TORNADO OR TWO ARE EXPECTED AS STORMS DEVELOP AND MOVE SOUTHEASTWARD ACROSS THE THREAT AREA.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: STRONG THUNDERSTORMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP AND INTENSIFY AHEAD OF A VIGOROUS MID LEVEL SHORTWAVE AND UPPER LEVEL JET STREAK. THE ENVIRONMENT AHEAD OF THIS SHORTWAVE...CURRENTLY LOCATED OVER MANITOBA...IS CHARACTERIZED BY MLCAPES GENERALLY AT OR ABOVE 2000 J/KG AND EFFECTIVE DEEP LAYER BULK SHEAR AT OR ABOVE 45 KTS. THIS ENVIRONMENT WILL SUPPORT VIGOROUS SUPER CELLULAR STORMS CHARACTERIZED BY VERY LARGE HAIL AND LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS..WITH THE WIND THREAT POTENTIALLY ENHANCED BY HIGH LCL HEIGHTS AND RELATIVELY LARGE LOW LEVEL TEMPERATURE-DEWPOINT SPREADS. THE RELATIVELY HIGH LCL HEIGHTS COMBINED WITH 0-1KM SHEAR LESS THAN 15 KTS...WILL LIMIT THE TORNADO THREAT...BUT A BRIEF TORNADO IS POSSIBLE WITH THE STRONGEST STORMS. INITIALLY DISCRETE SUPERCELLS WILL DEVELOP AND MOVE SOUTHEASTWARD WITH UPSCALE GROWTH INTO DAMAGING BOW ECHO STRUCTURES POSSIBLE.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE THREAT FOR TORNADOES AND DAMAGING WIND GUSTS CONTINUES ACROSS THE WATCH AREA.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SURFACE ANALYSIS SHOWS PRESSURE FALLS CONCENTRATED OVER FROM FAR ERN VA TOWARD DE. RADAR TRENDS HAVE BEEN UPWARD OVER THE PAST HOUR OR TWO WITH A SUPERCELLS AND POSSIBLE BRIEF TORNADOES ONGOING ACROSS THE DELMARVA. THIS GENERALLY N-S ORIENTED LINE OF STORMS WILL CONTINUE TO POSE A TORNADO THREAT AS THEY MOVE ACROSS THE BAY. THE MOST NOTABLE STORMS WERE ALONG THE WARM FRONT AND WILL HAVE ACCESS TO THE STRONGEST SHEAR. THE DOX VWP SHOWS A LARGE HODOGRAPH LOOP WITH 300 M2/S2 0-1 KM SRH...ALTHOUGH PART OF THAT IS INEFFECTIVE DUE TO THE COOLER SFC TEMPERATURES. RELATIVELY COMPLEX STORM MODES AND INTERACTIONS SUGGEST TORNADOES WILL BE BRIEF. ..JEWELL.. 06/27/2015 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE AREA IS BEING MONITORED FOR AN INCREASING RISK OF SVR TSTMS THIS AFTERNOON WITH A FEW SVR WIND GUSTS POSSIBLE. HOWEVER...CONFIDENCE IN MORE THAN A MODEST-COVERAGE SVR EVENT IS LIMITED AT THIS TIME...AND WW ISSUANCE IS PRESENTLY UNLIKELY.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY AND MOSAIC RADAR LOOPS INDICATE CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT UNDERWAY ALONG THE MOGOLLON RIM TO THE WHITE MOUNTAINS AND INTO THE MOUNTAINS OF SERN AZ NEAR TUCSON. THIS ACTIVITY IS DEVELOPING IN THE DIURNALLY HEATED/WELL MIXED BOUNDARY LAYER AMIDST PW BETWEEN 1.0 AND 1.3 INCHES PER GPS DATA. STRONG SFC HEATING IS FACILITATING THE DEVELOPMENT OF MODERATE INSTABILITY...WHICH MAY ALLOW FOR UPDRAFTS TO INTENSIFY AS THEY SPREAD WWD...AND WSWWD OFF THE RIM. WITH DCAPE AROUND 1200-1600 J/KG IN THE WELL/DEEPLY MIXED PBL...CONFIDENCE IS INCREASING THAT STRONG OUTFLOW WINDS WILL BE OF CONCERN. A FEW ISOLATED SVR WIND GUSTS MAY ALSO OCCUR...PARTICULARLY IF LOCALIZED COLD POOLS AMALGAMATE AND FOSTER MESO-BETA-SCALE ENHANCEMENTS TO THE LOW-LEVEL WIND THREAT. THIS MAY BE BECOMING EVIDENT WITH ACTIVITY SPREADING SW OF THE WHITE MOUNTAINS...THAT COULD AFFECT THE TUCSON AREA IN THE NEXT FEW HOURS. THE EMX VWP SAMPLES 10-15-KT ELYS IN THE LOWEST 6 KM AGL...WHICH MAY INDEED SUPPORT WWD MOVING COLD POOLS SPREADING ACROSS THE DESERT FLOOR INTO THE LATE AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING -- PERHAPS AFFECTING THE PHOENIX AREA BY EARLY EVENING. HOWEVER...WITHOUT STRONGER DEEP SHEAR IN PLACE...AND WITHOUT HIGHER CONFIDENCE IN UPSCALE CONVECTIVE GROWTH...WW ISSUANCE IS PRESENTLY UNLIKELY...THOUGH TRENDS WILL BE MONITORED THROUGH THE EVENING.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THUNDERSTORM COVERAGE WILL INCREASE ACROSS PARTS OF NORTH-CENTRAL AND NORTHEAST SD OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS AND SPREAD TOWARD PARTS OF SOUTHWEST MN. THESE STORMS WILL BE CAPABLE OF STRONG TO LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS...AND THE AREA IS BEING MONITORED FOR WATCH ISSUANCE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: STORMS ARE CURRENTLY APPROACHING THE ND/SD STATE BORDER AND ADDITIONAL DEVELOPMENT IS EVIDENT IN RADAR AND SATELLITE DATA ALONG THE COLD FRONT IN NORTH-CENTRAL SD. WHILE INSTABILITY IS NOT QUITE AS STRONG AS FURTHER NORTH DUE TO POORER SURFACE DEWPOINTS...IT IS CERTAINLY SUFFICIENT FOR CONTINUED DEVELOPMENT. FURTHERMORE...EFFECTIVE SHEAR WILL AID IN MAINTENANCE AND ORGANIZATION OF ANY STORMS THAT DEVELOP ACROSS THE AREA. POOR MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES WILL LIMIT VIGOROUS UPDRAFTS AND HENCE LARGE HAIL PRODUCTION. BUT...LARGE TEMPERATURE-DEW POINT SPREADS...RESULTING IN STEEP LOW LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND DCAPE VALUES BETWEEN 1000-1500 J/KG WILL AID IN STRONG TO LOCALLY DAMAGING WIND POTENTIAL. THE AREA IS BEING MONITORED FOR POSSIBLE WATCH ISSUANCE BY 23Z.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AT LEAST SCATTERED THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT IS EXPECTED TO CONTINUE TO DEVELOP ACROSS MUCH OF THE REGION THROUGH MID TO LATE EVENING. DAMAGING WIND GUSTS APPEAR THE PRIMARY THREAT IN STRONGER STORMS. THE POTENTIAL FOR UPSCALE CONVECTIVE GROWTH INTO AN EVOLVING MESOSCALE CONVECTIVE SYSTEM REMAINS UNCLEAR...BUT SEEMS LOW AT THIS POINT. UNLESS THIS OCCURS...THE SEVERE WIND POTENTIAL MAY REMAIN SOMEWHAT SPOTTY IN NATURE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: DUE TO GENERALLY WEAK LOWER/MID TROPOSPHERIC LAPSE RATES AND LIMITED SURFACE HEATING...MIXED LAYER CAPE ACROSS MUCH OF THE REGION IS RATHER MODEST...TO THE SOUTH OF A CONVECTIVELY REINFORCED FRONTAL ZONE ACROSS THE EASTERN VIRGINIA PANHANDLE AND NORTHERN VIRGINIA INTO THE DELMARVA PENINSULA. ASIDE FROM A CORRIDOR OF STRONGER HEATING TO AROUND 90F ACROSS THE SOUTH CAROLINA PIEDMONT...WHERE CAPE MAY BE IN EXCESS OF 2000 J/KG... VALUES APPEAR GENERALLY ON THE ORDER OF 1000-1500 J/KG ELSEWHERE. IN THE WAKE OF THE CONVECTIVE BAND NOW SPREADING INTO/THROUGH THE DELMARVA PENINSULA...SOUTHERLY 850 MB FLOW /AND LOW-LEVEL SHEAR/ IS FAIRLY WEAK. BUT SOUTHWESTERLY MID-LEVEL FLOW IS AT LEAST MODEST IN STRENGTH /30-40 KT AROUND 500 MB/....AHEAD OF A SIGNIFICANT SHORT WAVE TROUGH GRADUALLY PIVOTING THROUGH THE OHIO VALLEY. AS THIS IMPULSE APPROACHES THE CENTRAL APPALACHIANS LATER THIS EVENING...MODELS SUGGEST THAT IT WILL TAKE ON AN INCREASINGLY NEUTRAL TO NEGATIVE TILT. FORCING ASSOCIATED WITH THIS FEATURE...COUPLED WITH SEASONABLY STRONG DEEP LAYER SHEAR... WILL CONTINUE TO PROVIDE AT LEAST SOME POTENTIAL FOR STRONG/SEVERE STORM DEVELOPMENT...INCLUDING ISOLATED SUPERCELLS. GIVEN THE MOIST NATURE OF THE BOUNDARY LAYER...AND PERHAPS SOME DRYING IN MID-LEVELS...HEAVY PRECIPITATION LOADING AND EVAPORATIVE COOLING NEAR DOWNDRAFTS MAY CONTRIBUTE TO THE RISK FOR STRONG SURFACE GUSTS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE TORNADO THREAT WILL CONTINUE ACROSS FAR EASTERN ND INTO NORTHWEST MN. STRONG WINDS AND SOME HAIL MAY ALSO ACCOMPANY THESE STORMS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THE VWP FROM THE MVX RADAR INDICATES A RATHER IMPRESSIVE LOW LEVEL HODOGRAPH CURRENTLY WITH 0-1 KM SRH NEAR 250 M2/S2. SUPERCELLS WITH A THREAT FOR TORNADOES...HAIL AND WIND WILL CONTINUE TO BE A CONCERN ACROSS THE WATCH AREA AS STORMS TRACK TO THE SOUTH/SOUTHEAST. FURTHER TO THE SOUTHEAST TOWARD CENTRAL MN...LOW LEVEL MOISTURE BECOMES RATHER POOR WITH DEWPOINTS IN THE LOW TO MID 50S RESULTING IN A SHARP DECLINE IN INSTABILITY. AS THE STORMS REACH THE EASTERN/SOUTHEASTERN EDGES OF WATCH 365 IN THE NEXT FEW HOURS A GRADUAL WEAKENING TREND IS EXPECTED. ..LEITMAN.. 06/27/2015 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ALTHOUGH THUNDERSTORM ACTIVITY COULD WEAKEN AS IT OVERSPREADS THE GREATER PHOENIX METROPOLITAN AREA...LIKELY DURING THE 01-03Z TIME FRAME...STRONG...POTENTIALLY DAMAGING...SURFACE GUSTS WILL STILL BE POSSIBLE
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: GENERALLY LIGHT NORTHEASTERLY/EASTERLY MID-LEVEL FLOW CONTINUES TO SUPPORT THUNDERSTORM PROPAGATION OFF THE HIGHER TERRAIN TO THE NORTHEAST AND EAST OF THE GREATER PHOENIX METROPOLITAN AREA. CONVECTION AND ASSOCIATED COLD POOLS APPEAR TO BE IN THE PROCESS OF CONSOLIDATING AND COULD...AT LEAST BRIEFLY...INTENSIFY DURING THE NEXT HOUR OR SO. BASED ON THE LATEST VWP DATA FROM PHOENIX...SYSTEM RELATIVE INFLOW UP TO 30 KT APPEARS POSSIBLE AS THE CONGLOMERATE COLD POOL BEGINS TO APPROACH PHOENIX. HOWEVER...IT REMAINS UNCLEAR FROM FORECAST SOUNDINGS WHETHER THE DEEPLY MIXED BOUNDARY LAYER OVER THE LOWER DESERTS IS CHARACTERIZED BY SUFFICIENT CAPE TO MAINTAIN VIGOROUS THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT. REGARDLESS...STRONG WIND GUSTS APPROACHING OR PERHAPS BRIEFLY EXCEEDING SEVERE LIMITS APPEAR POSSIBLE WITH EVEN WEAKENING CONVECTION AS IT OVERSPREADS THE PHOENIX AREA DURING THE 01-03Z TIME FRAME.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: CONTINUED WEAKENING OVER THE NEXT 1-2 HOURS IS EXPECTED WITH THE CLUSTER OF STORMS FROM FAR SOUTHEAST ND INTO NORTHWEST MN AND PARTS OF NORTHEAST SD. AN OCCASIONAL STRONG WIND GUST OR MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL STONE WILL BE POSSIBLE THROUGH 03Z IN AND NEAR THE EXISTING WATCH AREAS...BUT NEW DOWNSTREAM WATCHES ARE NOT EXPECTED AT THIS TIME.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A GRADUAL WEAKENING TREND HAS BEEN EVIDENT ACROSS TORNADO WATCH 365 AND SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH 366 OVER THE LAST 45 MINUTES OR SO. THIS SHOULD CONTINUE AS STORMS TRACK SOUTHEAST INTO A POOR THERMODYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT. SPORADIC/ISOLATED SEVERE WIND/HAIL MAY STILL OCCUR FOR ANOTHER 1-2 HOURS...BUT THE OVERALL SEVERE THREAT APPEARS TO BE DIMINISHING AS THE BOUNDARY LAYER BECOMES INCREASINGLY STABLE. ANY STORMS THAT DEVELOP BEHIND THE COLD FRONT OR IN THE WAKE OF THE MAIN CLUSTER OF CONVECTION WILL BE ELEVATED AND SEVERE THREAT WILL BE MINIMAL. DOWNSTREAM WATCHES ARE NOT ANTICIPATED AT THIS TIME.
